subject: SummitHealth pilot: scope, success gates & SDK routes

Subject: SummitHealth pilot: scope, success gates & SDK routes

Hi Alex / Priya — great to meet earlier. Recap + proposed next steps from our discovery call so we have alignment before we kick off the pilot.

Quick summary of what we heard: 
- Goal: Evaluate Redwood inference for clinical note summarization and triage routing inside SummitHealth’s patient intake flow.
- Primary success metrics: average latency < 400ms p50 on 512-token prompts, extractive summary accuracy >= 86% vs. annotated set, and < 0.5% unsafe output rate on safety evals.
- Data: all PII will be hashed before leaving SummitHealth environment; you’ll provide a sampled set (5k de-identified records) for offline evals.

Proposed POC plan (2 weeks):
1) Week 0 (this week): finalize success criteria doc and security checklist; exchange SOC2 evidence.
2) Week 1: integration sprint — connect API / SDK for synchronous generation and validate streaming for live triage.
3) Week 2: run acceptance tests (latency/accuracy/safety), review results, and decision meeting.

Ownership (suggested):
- Redwood: Stephanie (commercial lead) + Karthik (SDK/engineering owner) + Vivek (infra / private network setup)
- SummitHealth: Alex (product lead) + Priya (security/compliance)

Open questions we need from you to lock schedule:
- Confirm the 5k sample delivery date (ETA?).
- Any constraints on outbound IPs or VPN that we must plan for?
- Are streaming websocket connections acceptable, or do you require a proxy approach?

Attachments: I’ve attached an editable success criteria spreadsheet and a short integration_routes.md with recommended REST and streaming routes.

Next steps: If this looks good, confirm the sample ETA and we’ll schedule a kickoff with engineering (30–45 min) for Monday.

Thanks —
Steph

2) IP/VPN: we prefer to avoid opening inbound firewall holes. Can Redwood support outbound-only connections to your hosted endpoint, or do we need to arrange a temporary VPN?

Also, for the acceptance criteria, can we add a qualitative gate: "no clinically misleading summaries on the top 200 sampled cases"? That will be part of our regulatory review.

Appreciate it — can we lock the kickoff for Monday 2028-06-18 at 10:00 PT?

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: SummitHealth pilot: scope, success gates & SDK routes

Alex / Priya — looping in the integration details you asked for. Below are the recommended routes and behaviors for the pilot. This is meant to be low-friction so you can start testing within a day of sample delivery.

1) REST generation (synchronous): POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate- headers: Authorization: Bearer <API_KEY>, Content-Type: application/json- body: {"model": "rwd-1-large", "input": "<text>", "max_tokens": 512}

2) Streaming (websocket): wss://stream.redwood.ai/v1/stream- Connect with same API key in query param. Server streams chunks as JSON frames: {"type": "chunk", "token": "..."} and sends a final frame {"type": "done"}. - Retry behavior: client should re-establish a new connection and resume from last acknowledged token id. We return incremental token ids in frames to enable safe resume.

3) Partial responses and UI handling: treat chunk frames as optimistic render; final frame contains metadata: latency_ms, tokens_generated, safety_flags. If resume occurs, Redwood will stitch segments server-side when the new connection includes the last token id.

4) Tool-calling / structured output: we support function-like JSON output via the routes; include "response_format" parameter and Redwood will return structured JSON in the final frame. Example: "response_format": {"schema": "{\"summary\":\"string\"}"}.

5) Rate limits & quotas: pilot tier default is 60 requests/minute and 20 concurrent streams. We can increase for the pilot on request; we’ll track token usage and surface it in the console.

6) Auth & security: API keys scoped to the deal and rotation is supported via the console. For private VPC deployments we can generate short-lived token proxies.

I’ve dropped a short integration markdown into the thread attachments (integration_routes.md) with code snippets you can paste into your frontend. If you want, we can do a 20 min tech walkthrough during Monday’s kickoff to step through the socket lifecycle.

-Karthik

- Procurement: we will likely issue a short PO for the pilot. Can you send a DocuSign-friendly PO template and the billing contact?

Also: we want a canary plan post-PO if we move to production — a brief note outlining rollback and fallback model routing would be great.

Priya

- Canary / rollback: Vivek will draft a short canary and rollback note (model variant fallback + traffic split policy) and attach it to the acceptance doc ahead of decision meeting.

- Kickoff (engineering + security): Mon 2028-06-18 10:00 PT (30 min) — calendar invite sent.
- Mid-pilot check-in: Thu 2028-06-21 10:00 PT (15 min) — quick status + early metrics.
- Decision review: Fri 2028-06-30 09:00 PT (45 min) — acceptance review and procurement next steps.

Final action items:

Looking forward to the kickoff.

Best —
Steph
